# Configuration of components

<!-- Generated by `composer docs:reference` from the class docblocks. Do not edit. -->

Components are configured in a task by `class` (class name or registered
short name) and `config` (the options listed here):

```yaml
preProcessors:
  10:
    class: CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\SetValuesPreProcessor
    config:
      values:
        pid: 12
```

Initializers, filters, processors, converters and finishers also accept the
option `disable`: `true`, or a condition with `expression` or
`if.result.hasMessage`. Data sources are never disabled, data targets only if
they implement `DisableableInterface`. See
[Configuration of tasks and sets](README.md#disabling-components).

## Data sources

Key in the task: `source`

### DataSourceDBAL

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Dbal\DataSourceDBAL`

Reads records from a database table via Doctrine DBAL. Requires the package
doctrine/dbal.

Configuration:

- `table` (string, required): table name, optionally `schema.table`
- `connection` (string, default `default`): name of the connection in the
  connection provider
- `fields` (list of strings, default all fields): fields to read
- `where` (map of field => value): equality conditions combined with AND;
  null means IS NULL, a list of integers or strings means IN (...)
- `filter` (condition): further conditions, combined with `where` by AND:
  comparisons, NULL checks, `all`/`any`/`not` groups, relative dates and
  `exists`/`notExists` on a related table; see `Filter`
- `timezone` (string, IANA name, default: PHP's default time zone): time
  zone of the relative dates in `filter`
- `orderBy` (map of field => `ASC`|`DESC`): sort order; not together with
  `cursorField`
- `limit` (int): maximum number of records
- `cursorField` (string): a unique, sortable field, e.g. `uid`. Records are
  read in ascending order of this field, in pages of `pageSize` records,
  and an interrupted task continues after the last processed record. Must
  be one of `fields`, if fields are given.
- `pageSize` (int, default 1000): records per query with `cursorField`

### DataSourceCSV

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\File\DataSourceCSV`

Reads records from a CSV file, one record per row.

The file is read row by row, so large files are not held in memory. Empty
rows are skipped. A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is
removed. A row with more or fewer values than fields is skipped and
reported as error 1795200501 with its row number, or, with `strict`, ends
the task with a `ParseException`. Rows are counted in the file, including
the header and empty rows; a value with line breaks is part of one row.

The source is resumable: the cursor holds the number and the position of
the last record read, so an interrupted task continues after it.

Configuration:

- `file` (string, required unless `url`): location of the file, passed to
  the resource loader; with the default loader a path relative to the
  working directory
- `url` (string, required unless `file`): URL of the file; requires a
  resource loader that supports URLs, e.g. `HttpResourceLoader`
- `fields` (list of strings or comma-separated string): field names, in
  the order of the columns. Without `fields`, the first row holds the
  field names.
- `header` (bool, default true without `fields`, false with `fields`):
  whether the first row holds field names. With `fields` and `header:
  true`, `fields` name the columns and the first row is skipped. Without
  `fields` and with `header: false`, the fields are the column numbers,
  starting at 0.
- `delimiter` (string, default ','): one character
- `enclosure` (string, default '"'): one character
- `escape` (string, default '\'): one character, or '' for none
- `encoding` (string, default 'UTF-8'): encoding of the file, one of
  `UTF-8`, `ASCII`, `ISO-8859-1` to `ISO-8859-10`, `ISO-8859-13` to
  `ISO-8859-16`, `Windows-1251`, `Windows-1252`, `Windows-1254`, `CP850`
  (case-insensitive); values are converted to UTF-8. Encodings other than
  UTF-8 and ASCII require the PHP extension mbstring.
- `strict` (bool, default false): a row with a wrong number of values
  ends the task with a `ParseException` instead of being skipped
- `recordNumberField` (string): adds the number of the record (1 for the
  first row after the header) as this field, e.g. as source ID for the ID
  map

### DataSourceXML

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\File\DataSourceXML`

Reads records from an XML file, one record per element.

With `element`, the file is read element by element (`XMLReader`), so large
files are not held in memory. With `expression`, the whole document is
loaded and the records are selected with XPath.

Each record element is converted into an array: attributes in
`@attributes`, child elements as fields named by their local name (lists
for repeated elements, strings for elements with only text), and text next
to attributes or child elements in `@value`.

The source is resumable: the cursor is the number of the last record read.
A resumed task reads the file from the beginning again and skips the
records up to the cursor.

Configuration:

- `file` (string, required unless `url`): location of the file, passed to
  the resource loader; with the default loader a path relative to the
  working directory
- `url` (string, required unless `file`): URL of the file; requires a
  resource loader that supports URLs, e.g. `HttpResourceLoader`
- `element` (string, required unless `expression`): name of the record
  elements, e.g. `item`, or `prefix:item` with a prefix of `namespaces`.
  Without prefix, elements of any namespace match. Record elements must
  not be nested in each other.
- `expression` (string, required unless `element`): XPath expression
  selecting the record elements, e.g. `//channel/item`; other nodes it
  selects are skipped
- `namespaces` (map of prefix => URI): namespaces for `element` and
  `expression`
- `lists` (list of strings): local names of child elements that are always
  lists, so that a field has the same type in all records: also with one
  element, and an empty list if the record element has none
- `recordNumberField` (string): adds the number of the record (1 for the
  first) as this field, e.g. as source ID for the ID map

### DataSourceQueue

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Persistence\DataSourceQueue`

Reads up to `limit` new records from a queue and claims them. After the
task, the claimed items are marked as finished.

Configuration:

- `identifier` (string, required): the queue
- `limit` (int, default 10): items per run

### NullDataSource

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Persistence\NullDataSource`

Data source without records, e.g. for tasks that only run initializers or
finishers. Note that finishers run, but the target's `persistAll()` is not
called without records.

Configuration:

none.

## Pre-processors

Key in the task: `preProcessors`

### RelationListPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Dbal\RelationListPreProcessor`

Sets the IDs related to a record, read from a relation (MM) table, e.g. the
categories of an event. Combine with `ResolveReferencePreProcessor` to map
them to target IDs. Requires the package doctrine/dbal.

Runs one query per record. A record without ID gets an empty list (or '').

Configuration:

- `table` (string, required): relation table, optionally `schema.table`
- `targetField` (string, required): field that receives the IDs
- `connection` (string, default `default`): name of the connection in the
  connection provider
- `idField` (string, default `uid`): field of the record holding its ID
- `localField` (string, default `uid_local`): column referring to the record
- `foreignField` (string, default `uid_foreign`): column with the related ID
- `sortField` (string, default `sorting`): order of the IDs; '' for none
- `where` (map of field => value): further conditions, e.g. `fieldname`
- `separator` (string): if set, the IDs are joined to a string; otherwise
  the field receives a list

### AddArraysPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\AddArraysPreProcessor`

Appends the values of array fields to a target field. Keys of the source
arrays are dropped, keys already in the target field are kept. Fields that
are missing or contain no array are skipped. A target value that is not an
array becomes the first element.

Moved from AddArrays of t3import_export.

Configuration:

- `targetField` (string, required): name of the target field
- `fields` (list or comma-separated string, required): source fields

### CleanPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\CleanPreProcessor`

Cleans string fields with PHP string functions. The options are applied in
the order of OPTIONS, independent of their order in the configuration.
Values that are no string and fields that are missing are kept.

Moved from Clean of t3import_export.

Configuration:

- `fields` (map of field => options, required, not empty). Options:
  - `str_replace`: `{search: string, replace: string}`
  - `stripslashes`, `strip_emptytags` (removes empty HTML elements),
    `strip_tags`, `htmlspecialchars`, `strip_spaces` (removes all
    whitespace), `trim`, `ltrim`, `rtrim`, `strtolower`, `strtoupper`:
    enabled unless the value is false

### EvaluateExpressionsPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\EvaluateExpressionsPreProcessor`

Sets fields of the record from expressions (Symfony ExpressionLanguage).

The fields are evaluated in the configured order. Each expression gets the
variable `record`, which contains the values of fields set before.

Configuration:

- `fields` (map of field => expression, required, not empty): the expressions

### ImplodeArrayPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\ImplodeArrayPreProcessor`

Joins the values of an array field to a string, e.g. a list read from XML.
With `child`, the array in that key of the field is joined; a string in that
key replaces the field. Keys are dropped. Fields that are missing or contain
no array (or no `child`) are kept.

Moved from ImplodeArray of t3import_export.

Configuration:

- `fields` (map of field => options, required, not empty). Options:
  - `child` (string): key of the array inside the field
  - `wrap` (string, default ','): separator

### SetValuesPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\SetValuesPreProcessor`

Sets fields to constant values, e.g. a record type or a storage page.
Existing values are replaced.

Configuration:

- `values` (map of field => scalar or null, required, not empty): the values

### StringToTimePreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\StringToTimePreProcessor`

Converts date strings to Unix timestamps with `strtotime()` (PHP's default
time zone). Values that are no string or cannot be parsed, and fields that
are missing, become null.

Moved from StringToTime of t3import_export.

Configuration:

- `fields` (list or comma-separated string, required): fields to convert
- `multipleRowFields` (list or comma-separated string): fields holding a
  list of child rows; the fields in `fields` are converted in each child row

### UnsetEmptyFieldsPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\UnsetEmptyFieldsPreProcessor`

Removes fields whose value is empty in the sense of PHP's `empty()`:
null, '', '0', 0, 0.0, false and [].

Moved from UnsetEmptyFields of t3import_export. Note that
`ValueRulesPreProcessor` considers only missing fields, null and '' empty.

Configuration:

- `fields` (list or comma-separated string, required): fields to check

### ValueRulesPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Processor\ValueRulesPreProcessor`

Applies declarative rules to the field values of a record, in order.
Covers the TypoScript rules of t3import_export used in imports: fallback (`teaser // abstract`), default value, copy and
rename (MapFields), value mapping (MapFieldValues), remove (RemoveFields),
trim, wrap and join (ConcatenateFields). No expressions, so no code from a pipeline is executed.

A value is empty if the field is missing, null or ''. Every rule may have a
condition `when`: `{field, equals}`, `{field, in}` or `{field, empty}`.

Configuration:

- `rules` (list of rules, required, not empty), each with `rule`:
  - `fallback`: `field` empty -> first non-empty value of the fields `from`
  - `default`: `field` empty -> `value`
  - `copy`: `field` = value of `from`
  - `rename`: `field` = value of `from`, `from` removed
  - `map`: `field` = `values[current]`; unmapped values are kept, or
    replaced by `otherwise` if given
  - `remove`: the fields `fields` are removed. A name with dots is a path
    into nested arrays, `*` stands for every element of a list:
    `address.street`, `children.*.hidden`. A field whose name is the
    whole path is removed instead
  - `trim`: whitespace around the string in `field` is removed
  - `wrap`: `field` not empty -> `prefix` . value . `suffix` (both default '')
  - `join`: `field` = non-empty values of the fields `from`, joined by
    `separator` (default ' ')

### ResolveReferencePreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\State\Component\ResolveReferencePreProcessor`

Replaces source IDs in a field with the target IDs from the ID map, e.g. the
parent page of a page or the category of an event.

The field may also hold a list of IDs. Empty values (`null`, `''`, `0`) are
left unchanged.

Configuration:

- `field` (string, required): field holding the reference
- `namespace` (string, required): namespace of the referenced records in
  the ID map
- `separator` (string): for fields holding several IDs as a string, e.g. `,`
- `onMissing` (string, default `fail`): what happens if a referenced ID has
  no mapping: `fail` throws an exception, `keep` keeps the source ID,
  `empty` removes it. `keep` and `empty` log a warning.

### TargetIdPreProcessor

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\State\Component\TargetIdPreProcessor`

Upsert by ID map: sets the target ID of a record written in an earlier run,
so the target updates that record instead of inserting it again.

The source ID is looked up in the ID map. If there is a mapping, its target
ID is set in `targetIdField`. Otherwise `targetIdField` is removed, so a
source ID never reaches the target ID column and the target inserts the
record. Use together with the `idMap` settings of the task and a target
that updates by `targetIdField`, e.g. `DataTargetDBAL` with that field as
`key` and `idField`.

The source ID is read before `targetIdField` is changed, so both may be the
same field.

Configuration:

- `namespace` (string, required): namespace of the records in the ID map
- `sourceIdField` (string, required): field holding the source ID
- `targetIdField` (string, default: `sourceIdField`): field for the target ID

## Filters

Key in the task: `filters`

### UnchangedRecordFilter

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\State\Component\UnchangedRecordFilter`

Incremental mode: skips records that were written before and did not change
since. A record is unchanged if the ID map holds a mapping for its source ID
with the checksum of the record (IdMapping::recordChecksum()).

Records without a source ID are accepted.

The filter runs after the pre-processors: the checksum covers the
pre-processed record, so changes in values that pre-processors add, e.g.
relation lists or resolved references, are detected. The source ID is taken
from the record as read from the source. Converters and post-processors are
not covered: after changing them, run the task without this filter once.

Configuration:

- `namespace` (string, required): namespace of the records in the ID map,
  as in the `idMap` settings of the task
- `sourceIdField` (string, required): field holding the source ID, as in
  the `idMap` settings of the task
- `targetIdField` (string): field in which `TargetIdPreProcessor` sets the
  target ID, as in the `idMap` settings of the task; required if it differs
  from `sourceIdField`, otherwise records are written once more after their
  first run

## Data targets

Key in the task: `target`

### DataTargetDBAL

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Dbal\DataTargetDBAL`

Writes records into a database table via Doctrine DBAL. Requires the package
doctrine/dbal.

Records must be arrays of column => scalar or null. With `key`, a record
updates the existing row with the same values in the key fields, if there
is one; otherwise it is inserted. A record without any of the key fields
is inserted, e.g. a new record after `TargetIdPreProcessor`.

Each batch is written in one transaction, committed in `flushBatch()`. If a
task fails, the rows of the current batch are not committed, and a resumed
run continues after the last committed batch.

Configuration:

- `table` (string, required): table name, optionally `schema.table`
- `connection` (string, default `default`): name of the connection in the
  connection provider
- `key` (list of strings): fields identifying an existing row, e.g.
  `['import_source', 'import_id']`. Without key, all records are inserted.
- `idField` (string, default `id`): primary key column. Its value is
  reported as target ID for the ID map: taken from the record, from the
  existing row on update, or from the generated ID after an insert. Set it
  to '' for tables without such a column; the target reports no IDs then.

### DataTargetCSV

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\File\DataTargetCSV`

Writes records into a CSV file, one row per record.

The file is created, or replaced, when the first record is written, and
closed in `persistAll()`. Records must be arrays. Values that are not
scalar are written as JSON; `Stringable` objects as string. Fields missing
in a record are written as empty values.

Configuration:

- `file` (string, required): path of the file, resolved by the path
  resolver; by default relative to the working directory. Missing
  directories are created.
- `fields` (list of strings or comma-separated string): fields to write,
  in this order; without `fields`, the fields of the first record
- `header` (bool, default true): writes the field names in the first row
- `delimiter` (string, default ','): one character
- `enclosure` (string, default '"'): one character
- `escape` (string, default '\'): one character, or '' for none
- `bom` (bool, default false): starts the file with a UTF-8 byte order
  mark, e.g. for spreadsheet applications

### DataTargetQueue

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Persistence\DataTargetQueue`

Writes records into a queue. Records that are already in the queue (same
checksum) are skipped, or set back to new with `allowUpdate`.

Configuration:

- `identifier` (string, required): the queue
- `allowUpdate` (bool, default false): records already in the queue are set
  back to new

### NullDataTarget

`CPSIT\ImportExportCore\Persistence\NullDataTarget`

Data target that does not write anything, e.g. for tasks whose finishers
use the result, or to try a configuration.

Configuration:

none.
